subject: Follow-up: DPA questions on controller roles, retention & logging
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cho <anna.cho@paygrid.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@paygrid.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: DPA questions on controller roles, retention & logging

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single place for next steps and your asks. Attaching our current DPA (redwood_dpa_v2.pdf) and a short SOC2 snapshot for context.

Key items you raised during the call:
- Clarify controller vs processor roles and what Redwood needs from PayGrid (what data we store/process and any required customer actions).
- Subprocessor transparency: can you confirm whether you require a maintained list in the DPA, and whether 30 days' notice is acceptable for new subprocessors?
- Breach notification SLAs: you mentioned a preference for 48 hours; we typically commit to 72 hours for initial notification. Is 72 a hard blocker?
- Data residency: requirement for EU-only processing for a subset of customers. Need to confirm hosted vs dedicated options.
- Logging & retention: PayGrid asked about request/response log retention (90 days vs 13 months) and whether we can provide redacted logs or field-level pseudonymization.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please send the DPA redline you want us to review (you mentioned Legal would circulate a redline).
2) I’ll loop in our Privacy lead (rafael_mendes) and Legal (evelyn_hart) to get definitive answers and suggested language for the addendum.
3) If any of the items above are blockers for procurement timing, flag them and we’ll prioritize.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v2.pdf, soc2-snapshot-2025.zip

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally and get back within 24 hours.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: Anna Cho <anna.cho@paygrid.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@paygrid.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 16:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA questions on controller roles, retention & logging

Camila — thanks for the recap and for sending the DPA. Attaching our redline (paygrid_dpa_redline.pdf). A few clarifying questions from Legal so we can turn our redline into a working version:

1) Controller vs Processor: we want an explicit statement that PayGrid is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor. We also need a short clause that describes limited cases where Redwood may act on its own (e.g., to comply with law enforcement or to remediate abuse). Is that acceptable?

2) Subprocessors: PayGrid requires a maintained list of subprocessors published to customers and asks for a 30-day notice period before onboarding a new subprocessor. Can Redwood agree to publish an up-to-date list and provide 30 days' notice?

3) Breach notification: our standard is initial notification within 48 hours of discovery for incidents impacting customer data. We understand there may be investigation time; can Redwood commit to 48 hours for initial notification, with follow-ups as more info becomes available?

4) Data residency: we need the ability to ensure EU-only processing for our EU customers. For hosted services, can you guarantee data processing in EU regions only? What are the constraints and lead time?

5) Logging & retention: PayGrid's compliance team prefers 13 months for certain request logs (access/drift logs). If Redwood's default is 90 days, can you offer 13 months as an add-on or provide an agreement to purge logs on request? Also: can you supply logs with PII redacted by default?

We are hoping to have a DPA in place by the end of next week to keep procurement on schedule. Please let me know if any of the items above are non-starters.

Thanks,
Anna Cho
Senior Counsel, Privacy 
PayGrid Inc.
anna.cho@paygrid.com
Attachment: paygrid_dpa_redline.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PayGrid DPA redline & Qs — need answers for procurement

Camila / Evelyn — below are draft answers and suggested language we can send to PayGrid. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to review verbatim.

1) Controller vs Processor- Short answer: Redwood will be Processor; PayGrid is Controller. Suggested clause: "Customer is the Controller and determines the purposes and means of processing. Redwood Inference acts as Processor and processes Customer Data solely on Customer's documented instructions, except as required by law (in which case Redwood will notify Customer where permitted)."

Notes: We avoid dual-role language where possible. For features that require Redwood to take action (safety remediation, legal compliance), include an exceptions paragraph. Evelyn — can you confirm the exact wording for the legal carve?

2) Subprocessors- Redwood publishes an up-to-date list of subprocessors at https://www.redwood.ai/subprocessors and will provide notice of material changes. Proposed contract language: "Redwood will maintain a current list of Subprocessors and provide Customer with written notice at least 30 days prior to engaging any new Subprocessor. Customer may reasonably object to a new Subprocessor within the notice period."

Common subprocessors (for context): AWS (us-east-1), GCP (europe-west4 for EU deployments), FastCache Inc. (managed KV cache), LogStore LLC (optional logging add-on). We can provide a hosted-only list vs dedicated/private lists if PayGrid needs detail.

3) Breach notification- We can commit to an initial notification within 72 hours of confirmation of a material security incident affecting Customer Data. Operationally, 48 hours is often tight for triage and preventing misleading notifications. Suggested compromise language: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide initial notification within 48 hours of confirming a material security incident, and in any event no later than 72 hours of discovery; follow-up updates will be provided as further information becomes available."

If PayGrid insists on a guaranteed 48-hour contractual commitment, we should mark this an escalation to Ops and discuss potential SOC/insurance/pricing implications.

4) Data residency- Options:
- Hosted (standard): Customers may select the region for processing (US, EU) at account setup, subject to capacity. For hosted customers we can route to EU region only, but there is a provisioning lead time (typically 5-10 business days) and some features (cross-region backups, SSO integrations) may still require metadata routing to US for control-plane traffic (we can document these).
- Dedicated / Private: Full EU-only deployments available; we can provide a Private control plane and on-prem package for strict residency requirements.

Suggested language for clarity: "Customer may elect EU-only processing for Customer Data where Redwood offers an EU processing region; Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to process and store Customer Data exclusively within the elected region, except for ancillary control-plane metadata and where required by law."

5) Logging & retention- Default: request-level logs (request ID, timestamps, model + cost metrics) retained 90 days. Options:
- 13-month retention add-on: available as a paid add-on and subject to a separate data storage fee.
- PII handling: Redwood will by default redact obvious PII from retained logs where feasible. However, we cannot guarantee automatic redaction for all customer-supplied content; customers should avoid sending direct identifiers unless needed. We can offer field-level pseudonymization guidance and work with PayGrid on ingestion filters.

Suggested contract snippet for retention: "Redwood will retain request logs for 90 days by default. Extended retention (13 months) is available as an optional service subject to additional fees; Customer may request deletion of logs earlier in accordance with the DPA."

Attachments to propose to PayGrid: redwood_dpa_v2.pdf (current language), SOC2 snapshot, and a short one-page addendum summarizing the 72h/48h compromise. I'll draft the one-pager if you want.

Summary recommendation: send PayGrid a response that 1) confirms Processor status, 2) agrees to publish subprocessors with 30-day notice, 3) proposes the 48/72 compromise language for breach notification, 4) explains hosted vs dedicated EU options and lead times, and 5) offers a 13-month retention add-on with pricing to follow.

Camila — if you agree, I can turn these into redlined language and return a short DPA addendum for Anna's team by EOD today.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
